platforms.name: Codex
platforms.note: SQLite state with threads, goals, queue, memories, spawn edges, and remote-control enrollments. Curated plugins for browser, computer use, documents, and review.

platforms.name: Claude Code
platforms.note: Per-project transcripts and auto-memory with a MEMORY.md index. Allow and deny lists for tools, agents, commands, skills, and a plugin marketplace.

platforms.name: GitHub Copilot
platforms.model: catalog refreshed by the agent host
platforms.note: Two stores: the CLI home with sessions, events, and permissions, and the editor's agent host with changesets, review, checkpoints, delegation, and Mission Control.

platforms.name: Gemini CLI
platforms.note: A thin CLI: trust, history, an empty MCP file, GEMINI.md instructions walked upward, and designed but unused memory paths.

platforms.name: Antigravity
platforms.note: A trajectory engine: one SQLite file per conversation with steps, nesting, battle mode, annotations, brain, and knowledge. A different product from Gemini CLI.

platforms.name: Grok
platforms.note: The fullest memory pipeline on the machine: capture, observations, consolidation, tombstones, and a chunk index. Bundled skills, roles, personas, and .rhai workflows.

platforms.name: Hermes
platforms.note: Routed and multi-channel: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Teams. Cron, kanban, shared rooms, delegation limits, a Docker terminal path, and a user profile.

platforms.name: Qwen
platforms.note: Points at the local Ollama host. Instruction files at global, team, and local scope, run limits by turns, time, and tool calls, and designed memory paths.

platforms.name: Ollama
platforms.model: deepseek-coder, gemma3, llama3.2, mistral, phi4, vrai-*
platforms.note: The model host, not an agent client. Weights, a REPL prompt history, and custom models built from Modelfiles. No session, grant, or memory service.

areas.name: Session & Turn
areas.description: Ability to hold a conversation with the agent as a durable, resumable record, run each turn inside it under the user's control, and recover it after interruption, across every surface the platform offers.
areas.scope: Covers the session record, the turn loop, in-flight control, continuity, and recovery. Excludes what the agent is told before a turn (Memory) and what it is allowed to do during one (Authority & Configuration).

capabilities.name: Session Store
capabilities.description: Ability to record every conversation durably, bound to a workspace, with its transcript, attachments, and external references, so it can be found and reopened later.
capabilities.scope: Inside: the catalog entry, the transcript, the workspace binding, attachments, and typed references. Excludes resuming or searching the record (Continuity) and the turn that writes it (Turn Loop).

services.name: Session Catalog
services.evidence: Cx threads · Cl projects · Cp session-store · Ge history · Ag Gk He Qw
services.description: A searchable list of every conversation, with identity and timestamps.

profile.inside: The list of conversations: one entry per session with its identity, workspace, title, repository, and timestamps, indexed for listing and lookup.
profile.excludes: The transcript's content (Transcript Log), which sessions are open (Resume Set), and full-text search over turns (Session Search).
profile.purpose: Lets a person or program find any past conversation and lets every other session service key its data to a stable session identity.
functions: Creates the entry when a session starts, assigning its identifier and recording the workspace it is bound to.
Returns sessions by workspace, repository, recency, or identifier for the command line, the editor, and protocol clients.
Keeps the title, turn count, and last-activity time current as turns complete.
entities: Session
One conversation. Attributes: session id, workspace path, repository, branch, title or summary, client name, created and updated timestamps, turn count, fork count.
Catalog Index
The lookup structure over sessions. Attributes: keys by workspace, repository, and recency.
inbound: creates the entry on the first turn and updates summary fields as turns complete
supplies the workspace path the session is keyed to
registers the child session and links it to its parent
outbound: the sessions to reopen on restart
the session identities the search index is keyed to
the running and recent sessions to display
profile.security: Entries name local paths and repositories, so the catalog is user-private and never leaves the machine except through Transcript Export or Audit Export.
profile.storage: A single local index file or database in the platform home, one per user.
profile.performance: Listing stays under 100 ms at 10,000 sessions; a lookup by identifier is constant time.

services.name: Transcript Log
services.evidence: Cx · Cl jsonl · Cp events.jsonl · Ge Qw chats · Ag steps · He messages
services.description: The append-only record of what was said and done in a session.

profile.inside: The ordered, append-only record of every message, tool call, tool result, permission event, and lifecycle event in a session.
profile.excludes: The session's identity and summary (Session Catalog), summaries written over the log (Progress Checkpoint), and its portable copy (Transcript Export).
profile.purpose: Gives the session a complete, replayable history that resume, search, audit, and compaction all read from.
functions: Writes one typed event at the end of the log with a timestamp and turn index.
Returns the events of a session in order so a client can rebuild its view or resume the model's context.
Closes a log on session end and protects it from edits.
entities: Transcript Event
One entry. Attributes: sequence, turn index, timestamp, type (user message, assistant message, tool call, tool result, permission, lifecycle), payload.
Transcript
The ordered set of events for one session. Attributes: session id, event count, first and last timestamps.
inbound: appends user, assistant, model, and lifecycle events as the turn runs
appends tool call and tool result events
appends permission requested and completed events
outbound: the events needed to rebuild context on resume
profile.security: Contains everything the user and tools said, including pasted content, so it is user-private; Secret Redaction runs before anything is written.
profile.storage: One append-only file per session in the platform home, line-oriented so a crash loses at most the last event.
profile.performance: Append is a single write under 5 ms; replay of a 10,000-event session completes under one second.

services.name: Workspace Binding
services.evidence: cwd on Cx Cl Cp Ge Ag Gk He Qw
services.description: The directory a session acts in, recorded so it can be resumed in place.

profile.inside: The association between a session and the directory it acts in, including how that directory is encoded in paths and keys.
profile.excludes: Whether the directory is trusted (Workspace Trust) and the repository's git state (Repository State).
profile.purpose: Makes a session resumable in place and lets every per-project store find its data by the same key.
functions: Records the working directory when a session begins.
Maps a directory to the stable key used by project memory, settings, and the catalog.
Updates the binding when a session is moved or its directory is renamed.
entities: Workspace
A directory a session acts in. Attributes: absolute path, encoded key, repository root if any.
inbound: the directory the client was launched in
outbound: the workspace path stored on the entry
the key that selects per-project configuration
the key that selects per-project memory
the folder to check before tools run
profile.security: A binding is a path, not a grant; it confers no permission by itself.
profile.storage: Stored on the catalog entry and encoded into the names of per-project directories.
profile.performance: Resolution is a pure function of the path; no I/O.

services.name: Attachment Store
services.evidence: Cp session files/ · Cp chats scratch dir
services.description: Files a session attached or produced, kept beside the transcript.

profile.inside: Files a session attached, pasted, or produced that are kept beside its transcript, including the scratch directory of a session with no workspace.
profile.excludes: Files edited in the workspace (File Edit, Edit Attribution) and memory notes (Topic Note).
profile.purpose: Keeps a session's non-transcript material addressable so a resume or export can bring it back.
functions: Saves a pasted or uploaded file under the session and returns a reference.
Writes a model-produced file to the session's directory.
Creates a working directory for sessions that have no workspace.
entities: Attachment
One stored file. Attributes: session id, name, content type, size, origin (pasted, uploaded, produced), path.
inbound: images and screenshots pasted into a turn
outbound: attachment content referenced by a turn
profile.security: Attachments may contain user data; they inherit the session's privacy and are removed with it.
profile.storage: A directory per session in the platform home.
profile.performance: Bounded by disk; a single attachment is limited to what the model can consume in one turn.

services.name: External Reference
services.evidence: Cp session_refs: issues, PRs
services.description: Issues, pull requests, and other typed links attached to a turn.

profile.inside: Typed links from a turn to things outside the session: issues, pull requests, documents, tickets.
profile.excludes: The pull request the agent itself opens (Pull Request Flow) and intake of an issue as work (Issue Intake).
profile.purpose: Lets a session record what it was about so the record can be found from the issue tracker side and so context can be re-fetched on resume.
functions: Records a typed reference with its identifier at a turn index.
Fetches the referenced object's current state through the host's interface when context is needed.
Finds sessions that touched a given issue or pull request.
entities: Reference
One link. Attributes: session id, turn index, type (issue, pull request, document), host, identifier, URL, title.
inbound: references mentioned or fetched during a turn
the issue a run was started from
outbound: the current state of a referenced object
profile.security: A reference holds an identifier, not the object's content; access to the object is checked by the host at resolve time.
profile.storage: A table or list keyed by session in the platform home.
profile.performance: Resolution is a network call to the host and is cached for the turn.

capabilities.name: Turn Loop
capabilities.description: Ability to execute one turn end to end: accept a prompt, call the model, dispatch tool calls, and return a response, with every step recorded.
capabilities.scope: Inside: the turn cycle and tool-call dispatch. Excludes the prompt's assembly (Briefing), the permission to run a tool (Execution Control), and the tools themselves (Native Tools).

services.name: Turn Execution
services.evidence: prompt in, model call, tool calls, response out · Cp turns table · Cx threads · Ag steps · AHP chat channel
services.description: One cycle of prompt, model call, tool calls, and response.

profile.inside: One full cycle: accept the assembled prompt, call the model, loop on tool calls until the model yields, and return the final response, recording each step.
profile.excludes: How the prompt is assembled (Prompt Assembly), how a tool call is routed (Tool Call Dispatch), and in-flight control (Turn Control).
profile.purpose: Is the unit of work every other service exists to prepare, bound, or record; the platform's core loop.
functions: Opens a turn against a session with the user's message and the assembled prompt.
Calls the model, hands tool requests to dispatch, feeds results back, and repeats until a final answer.
Emits the final response, usage, and a lifecycle event, and returns control to the surface.
entities: Turn
One request-response cycle. Attributes: session id, turn index, user message, assistant response, model, start and end timestamps, token usage, finish reason.
Model Call
One request to the model inside a turn. Attributes: turn index, call index, latency, cached tokens, reasoning effort.
inbound: the user's message that starts a turn
the prompt of a non-interactive run
the next queued message after a turn ends
outbound: each tool request from the model
summary updates when the turn completes
profile.security: Runs only inside a trusted workspace under the current Approval Mode; never bypasses dispatch to run a tool directly.
profile.storage: Holds state in memory for the duration of the turn; durable state is the transcript.
profile.performance: First token from the model within the provider's latency; the loop adds under 50 ms per tool round trip.

services.name: Tool Call Dispatch
services.evidence: Cp tool.execution events, tool-call tracker · Ag steps · ACP tool_call updates · every CLI
services.description: Routing a model's tool request to the right tool and returning the result.

profile.inside: Receiving a tool request from the model, resolving the tool, checking permission, invoking it, and returning a result the model can read.
profile.excludes: The tools themselves (Native Tools, MCP Server) and the policy decision (Approval Mode, Remembered Grant).
profile.purpose: Keeps a single, auditable path between the model's intent and anything that touches the machine.
functions: Matches the requested name to a native tool, a skill, or an MCP server's tool.
Asks Execution Control whether the call may run and records the answer.
Runs the tool with its arguments, applies output limits, and returns the result with an event record.
entities: Tool Call
One invocation. Attributes: turn index, call id, tool name, arguments, permission outcome, start and end timestamps, result size, status.
Tool Registry
The set of callable tools. Attributes: name, source (native, skill, MCP), schema.
inbound: a tool request from the model
tool definitions and results from configured servers
pre- and post-tool hooks that may block or amend the call
outbound: the question of whether to ask
profile.security: No tool runs without passing the gate; arguments are logged with Secret Redaction applied.
profile.storage: Stateless; the record lives in the transcript and the permission stream.
profile.performance: Dispatch overhead under 10 ms; tool output truncated to a fixed limit before it reaches the model.

capabilities.name: Turn Control
capabilities.description: Ability to interrupt, steer, question, and cap a turn while it runs, from the keyboard or over a protocol, without losing the session.
capabilities.scope: Inside: interrupt, mid-turn steering, questions to the user, and run limits. Excludes limits set by a plan or goal (Planning) and approvals of individual actions (Execution Control).

services.name: Turn Interrupt
services.evidence: Cl stream-json interrupt · Cx turn/interrupt · Cp SDK abort() · ACP session/cancel · AHP chat/turnCancelled
services.description: Stopping a running turn cleanly, from the keyboard or over a protocol.

profile.inside: Stopping a running turn cleanly on request: cancelling the model call, stopping tools, and leaving the session consistent.
profile.excludes: Steering without stopping (Message Steering) and limits that stop a run automatically (Run & Spend Limit).
profile.purpose: Gives the user and any client a reliable way to stop the agent without corrupting the session.
functions: Accepts a stop from the keyboard, a protocol message, or an SDK call.
Aborts the model stream and signals running tools to stop.
Records a cancelled lifecycle event and returns the session to idle.
entities: Interrupt
One stop request. Attributes: session id, turn index, source (keyboard, protocol, SDK), timestamp, outcome.
profile.security: Any party that can start a turn may stop it; no elevated right is needed.
profile.storage: None beyond the transcript event.
profile.performance: Acknowledged within 100 ms; running tools are given a bounded grace period before being killed.

services.name: Message Steering
services.evidence: AHP steering pending messages · Cl stream-json input mid-turn · Cl Cp hook additionalContext
services.description: Injecting guidance into a turn that is already running.

profile.inside: Delivering an additional user message or hook-supplied context into a turn that is already running, so the model sees it at the next step.
profile.excludes: Stopping the turn (Turn Interrupt) and messages that wait for the turn to end (Follow-up Queue).
profile.purpose: Lets the user correct course mid-turn instead of stopping and restarting.
functions: Accepts a message while a turn is running and marks it pending.
Adds the pending message to the model's context before the next model call.
Logs the message as a user event in the transcript.
entities: Pending Message
A message awaiting injection. Attributes: session id, turn index, text, source (user, hook), queued and delivered timestamps.
inbound: a message typed during a turn
outbound: the message to inject before the next model call
profile.security: Hook-supplied context is marked by origin so the model can tell it from the user's words.
profile.storage: In-memory queue for the turn.
profile.performance: Injected before the next model call; never delays the current call.

services.name: Human Input Request
services.evidence: Cl AskUserQuestion, Elicitation hook · ACP session/request_permission · AHP chat/inputRequested
services.description: The agent pausing to ask the user a question or for a decision.

profile.inside: The agent pausing a turn to ask the user a question or present a choice, and resuming with the answer.
profile.excludes: Permission prompts for individual tool calls (Permission Stream) and steering the user initiates (Message Steering).
profile.purpose: Lets the agent resolve ambiguity with the user instead of guessing.
functions: Presents a question with optional structured choices and suspends the turn.
Receives the user's answer from the surface and validates it against the choices.
Feeds the answer into the turn as a user message.
entities: Input Request
One question. Attributes: session id, turn index, prompt text, choices, answer, raised and answered timestamps, source surface.
inbound: a client's answer to an input request
outbound: a notice that the agent is waiting
profile.security: The answer is user input and is treated as such; a headless run with no surface to ask must fail the request rather than invent an answer.
profile.storage: Transcript only.
profile.performance: The turn waits indefinitely by default; a run limit may time it out.

services.name: Run & Spend Limit
services.evidence: Cl --max-budget-usd · Qw --max-session-turns, --max-wall-time, --max-tool-calls · Ag --print-timeout
services.description: A cap on turns, time, tool calls, or money for one run.

profile.inside: Caps on one run: maximum turns, wall time, tool calls, or spend, enforced while the run executes.
profile.excludes: The goal a run serves (Goal & Budget), the user's plan ceiling (Plan & Entitlement), and the interrupt a person issues (Turn Interrupt).
profile.purpose: Makes unattended runs safe to start by bounding what they can consume.
functions: Accepts limits from flags, settings, or a caller.
Counts turns, tool calls, elapsed time, and estimated spend as the run proceeds.
Ends the run with a recorded reason when any limit is reached.
entities: Run Limit
The caps for one run. Attributes: max turns, max wall time, max tool calls, max spend, source.
Run Meter
Current consumption. Attributes: turns, tool calls, elapsed seconds, spend to date.
outbound: the stop signal when a limit is reached
profile.security: A limit can be lowered by any caller and raised only by the user or an explicit flag.
profile.storage: In memory for the run; the outcome is in the transcript.
profile.performance: Metering adds no measurable latency; the stop is checked before each model call and tool call.

capabilities.name: Continuity
capabilities.description: Ability to resume, search, fork, summarize, and share sessions so work continues across restarts, days, and people.
capabilities.scope: Inside: the resume set, search, forks, progress checkpoints, and share links. Excludes delegation to child agents (Delegation), which is a different kind of fork.

services.name: Resume Set
services.evidence: Cp open-sessions, sidebar pins · Cx read receipts · Gk active_sessions · Ag presence
services.description: Which sessions are open or pinned, so they come back on restart.

profile.inside: The set of sessions that are open, pinned, or were active when the client last ran, so they are restored on the next start.
profile.excludes: The catalog of all sessions (Session Catalog) and the content being resumed (Transcript Log).
profile.purpose: Lets the user close the client and come back to the same work.
functions: Records which sessions are open and whether a turn was in flight.
Keeps a session in the sidebar or list for a workspace regardless of recency.
Reopens the recorded sessions on start and rebuilds their context from the transcript.
entities: Open Session Entry
One open or pinned session. Attributes: session id, workspace, opened and refreshed timestamps, working flag, order.
inbound: sessions opened and closed in the terminal
outbound: the events to replay on restore
the sessions to show on start
profile.security: Holds identifiers only.
profile.storage: A small state file per user, plus one per workspace for pinned order.
profile.performance: Restore of ten sessions completes within the client's start time.

services.name: Session Search
services.evidence: Cp FTS · Gk session_search
services.description: Full-text search across past transcripts.

profile.inside: A full-text index over session titles and transcript content, with queries that return matching sessions and turns.
profile.excludes: Searching memory (Memory Retrieval) and searching the codebase (Code Search).
profile.purpose: Lets the user find a past conversation by what was said in it.
functions: Adds new turns to the index as they are written.
Returns sessions and turns ranked by match.
Recreates the index from transcripts when it is missing or stale.
entities: Search Document
One indexed unit. Attributes: session id, turn index, text, timestamp.
Search Index
The full-text structure. Attributes: document count, last indexed sequence.
inbound: session metadata to attach to results
profile.security: Indexes user-private content; the index is as private as the transcripts and is deleted with them.
profile.storage: A full-text index in the platform home, rebuildable from transcripts.
profile.performance: A query over 100,000 turns returns in under 200 ms.

services.name: Session Fork
services.evidence: Cp fork_count · Cp workspace-fork lock
services.description: Branching a conversation into a child session.

profile.inside: Creating a child session from a point in an existing one, so two lines of conversation can continue separately.
profile.excludes: Handing work to a child agent (Subagent Delegation), which is agent-initiated and scoped to a task.
profile.purpose: Lets the user explore an alternative without losing the original thread.
functions: Copies the transcript up to a chosen turn into a new session.
Records the parent session and fork point on the child.
Prevents two forks from racing on the same parent record.
entities: Fork Edge
The link between parent and child. Attributes: parent session id, child session id, fork turn index, timestamp.
outbound: the new child entry with lineage
profile.security: A fork inherits the parent's workspace trust and permissions; it does not widen them.
profile.storage: The child has its own transcript; lineage is on the catalog entry.
profile.performance: Forking a 10,000-event session completes under one second.

services.name: Progress Checkpoint
services.evidence: Cp checkpoints: overview, work done, next steps
services.description: A written summary of work done and next steps at a point in time.

profile.inside: A written summary at a point in time: what was done, what matters, which files, and what comes next.
profile.excludes: The raw transcript (Transcript Log), file snapshots (File Rewind), and automatic context shrinking (Context Compaction).
profile.purpose: Lets a person or a resumed session pick up the work without rereading everything.
functions: Produces the summary from the transcript at the current turn.
Returns the session's checkpoints in order.
Supplies the latest checkpoint to a resumed session.
entities: Checkpoint
One summary. Attributes: session id, turn index, title, overview, work done, technical details, important files, next steps, timestamp.
inbound: a checkpoint requested at the end of a turn
outbound: the latest checkpoint for a resumed session
profile.security: A checkpoint is derived content and inherits the transcript's privacy.
profile.storage: Markdown beside the session and a structured row in the catalog.
profile.performance: Writing a checkpoint costs one model call.

services.name: Session Share Link
services.evidence: no home stores a shareable link to a session
services.description: A link that lets another person open a session.

profile.inside: A link that grants another person read or edit access to a session's record.
profile.excludes: Multi-user live collaboration (Shared Room) and exporting a file (Transcript Export).
profile.purpose: Lets a conversation be handed to a colleague without copying files.
functions: Generates a link with a scope (read or edit) and an optional expiry.
Opens the session for the holder under the link's scope.
entities: Share Link
One grant. Attributes: session id, token, scope, created and expiry timestamps, creator.
outbound: the session rendered for the link holder
profile.security: Links are bearer credentials: unguessable, expiring, and revocable; the transcript is redacted before it is shared.
profile.storage: Vendor-hosted, since the holder is not on the user's machine.
profile.performance: Open in under two seconds for a typical session.

capabilities.name: Recovery
capabilities.description: Ability to return a session and its files to a good state after a bad edit, an oversized context, or a need to archive or export, with nothing lost silently.
capabilities.scope: Inside: file rewind, context compaction, archive and erasure, and export. Excludes git-level undo (Change Set) and memory erasure (Pipeline).

services.name: File Rewind
services.evidence: Cp rewind-file-snapshots · Cl file-history
services.description: Restoring files to how they were before an agent edit.

profile.inside: Content-addressed snapshots of files before the agent edits them, and restoring any file or the whole set to a prior state.
profile.excludes: Git-level undo (Repository State, Worktree Isolation) and rewinding the conversation itself (Session Fork).
profile.purpose: Makes every agent edit reversible even when the workspace is not under version control.
functions: Stores the prior bytes of a file the first time a turn changes it.
Restores one file or all files touched since a chosen turn.
Discards snapshots when the session is archived.
entities: File Snapshot
Prior content of one file. Attributes: session id, turn index, path, content hash, size, timestamp.
profile.security: Snapshots can contain source and data; they stay under the session's directory and are removed with it.
profile.storage: Content-addressed blobs per session, deduplicated by hash.
profile.performance: Snapshot cost is one copy per touched file per turn.

services.name: Context Compaction
services.evidence: He compression · Cp compaction events, usage_checkpoint
services.description: Shrinking the context window by summarizing older turns.

profile.inside: Reducing a session's context window by summarizing older turns and replacing them with the summary, with the originals kept in the transcript.
profile.excludes: Choosing what enters the window in the first place (Context Budget) and human-readable checkpoints (Progress Checkpoint).
profile.purpose: Lets long sessions continue past the model's context limit without losing the thread.
functions: Watches token usage against the window size.
Produces a summary of older turns and swaps it into the live context.
Logs the compaction with the range it covered.
entities: Compaction Record
One compaction. Attributes: session id, from and to turn index, summary tokens, replaced tokens, timestamp.
outbound: the compacted context for the next call
profile.security: Summaries are model output and may paraphrase sensitive content; they stay with the session.
profile.storage: The summary lives in the live context and the event in the transcript.
profile.performance: One model call per compaction; triggered before the window overflows.

services.name: Archive & Erasure
services.evidence: Cp archives · Cp cleanup flags
services.description: Archiving or deleting sessions and their traces.

profile.inside: Moving a session out of the active set and, on request, deleting it with its transcript, attachments, snapshots, and index entries.
profile.excludes: Forgetting memory (Memory Erasure) and vendor-side data deletion (Data Use Consent).
profile.purpose: Keeps the active list small and lets the user remove what should not persist.
functions: Marks a session archived and hides it from default lists.
Deletes every local trace of a session and records the erasure.
Removes derived artifacts the platform no longer needs.
entities: Archive Record
One archived or erased session. Attributes: session id, action, timestamp, reason.
inbound: the session and its related stores
profile.security: Erasure is complete on the local machine; anything already exported or shared is out of scope and is said so.
profile.storage: Archived sessions stay in place; erased sessions leave only the archive record.
profile.performance: Erasure of a session completes within seconds regardless of size.

services.name: Transcript Export
services.evidence: no export store in any home
services.description: Writing a session out in a portable format.

profile.inside: Writing a session out as a portable file: markdown, JSON, or HTML, with attachments optionally bundled.
profile.excludes: Auditor-ready records (Audit Export) and links to the live session (Session Share Link).
profile.purpose: Lets a conversation leave the platform for documentation, review, or another tool.
functions: Produces the file in the chosen format from the transcript.
Applies secret redaction and optional path anonymization before writing.
Includes attachments and checkpoints when asked.
entities: Export
One exported file. Attributes: session id, format, path, redaction applied, timestamp.
profile.security: Redaction is on by default; exporting without it requires an explicit flag.
profile.storage: Written where the user asks; the platform keeps no copy.
profile.performance: Export of a 10,000-event session completes under five seconds.

areas.name: Authority & Configuration
areas.description: Ability to bound what the agent may do, as which identity, under which policy, and to configure that at user, project, and organization scope, with every grant recorded.
areas.scope: Covers admission, identity, execution control, and configuration. Excludes the tools themselves (Extension & Tools) and the model provider's own limits (Models).

capabilities.name: Admission
capabilities.description: Ability to decide which workspaces, content, and policies the agent may act under before any tool runs, with trust decisions recorded and organization policy enforced over user settings.
capabilities.scope: Inside: workspace trust, managed policy, content exclusion, and the untrusted-content guard. Excludes per-action approval (Execution Control) and who the agent is (Identity).

services.name: Workspace Trust
services.evidence: Cx trust_level · Cp trustedFolders · Ge · Ag · Gk decided_at
services.description: A recorded decision that the agent may act in a folder.

profile.inside: The recorded decision that the agent may act inside a folder, the prompt that asks for it, and the list of trusted folders.
profile.excludes: Per-action approvals (Approval Mode, Remembered Grant) and exclusion of files within a trusted folder (Content Exclusion).
profile.purpose: Stops the agent from acting in a directory the user has not deliberately opened to it.
functions: Asks the user the first time a folder is opened and records the answer with a timestamp.
Answers whether a path is inside a trusted folder before any tool runs.
Removes a folder from the trusted list.
entities: Trust Decision
One folder's status. Attributes: path, level (trusted, untrusted), decided timestamp, decided by.
inbound: the folder a session is bound to
the user's answer to the trust prompt
organization rules that force or forbid trust
outbound: whether the workspace permits tools at all
profile.security: Trust is per folder and per user; a parent folder's trust covers its children unless policy says otherwise.
profile.storage: A list in the user settings or a dedicated trust file in the platform home.
profile.performance: A path check is an in-memory prefix match.
